flow-definition.description:
Deploys HPDS auth, HPDS open and PSAMA (PIC-SURE Auth Micro App) with an already staged dataset to the STAGING stack, in one build. Normally started by HPDS Data - Stage to Stack Bucket when it runs with DEPLOY_TO_STAGING_STACK=true, which passes the three deploy keys. It can also be run by hand with the three keys (the keys printed by HPDS Data - Stage to Stack Bucket, or the blame commits of the source_dataset_s3_url, source_destigmatized_dataset_s3_url and source_genomic_dataset_s3_url lines of build-spec.json). There is no stack parameter and no default for any key.
Order of work: 1. The three keys are validated first (7 to 40 lowercase hex characters); a bad key fails the build before anything else happens. 2. Everything after that runs inside a time limit of 4 hours (timeout step). 3. The deployment-state lock is taken first, by building Retrieve Deployment State (S3 legal hold on deployment_state_metadata/stacks.json, the same lock Deployment Pipeline and Swap Stacks take). It fails fast: when the lock is held by another deployment this build fails at once, deploys nothing and does NOT run Unlock Deployment State (a lock this build did not take is never released). 4. The staging stack is environments.next_prod of the stacks.json that Retrieve Deployment State archived. It is the only stack this job reads; an empty, null or not plain name is refused. 5. The stack lock stack-<staging stack> (Lockable Resources, the same resource the PIC-SURE ... Build and Deploy jobs hold) is taken second and WAITS if a build of those jobs is running on the staging stack. While it waits (up to the time limit) the deployment-state lock is still held, so a Deployment Pipeline or Swap Stacks run started in that window fails at once; start it again afterwards. 6. Inside the stack lock the stack bucket is checked again: the auth dataset (data/<auth key>/javabins_rekeyed/manifest.tsv or the legacy data/<auth key>/javabins_rekeyed.tar), the open dataset (data/<open key>/destigmatized_javabins_rekeyed/manifest.tsv or the legacy .tar) and data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json. Anything missing fails the build and nothing is deployed. 7. Then, each started only after the one before ended SUCCESS: PIC-SURE HPDS Auth Deploy (auth key, genomic key), PIC-SURE HPDS Open Deploy (open key), PIC-SURE Auth Micro App Deploy (auth key; PSAMA copies data/<auth key>/fence_mapping.json into its container when it starts, so it is redeployed with the dataset). Each gets TARGET_STACK = the staging stack; their other parameters keep their defaults (the stack bucket). 8. Whatever happens after the deployment-state lock was taken (a failed deploy, the time limit, an abort), the build runs Unlock Deployment State at the end. stacks.json is not changed, so Write Stack State is not run. If the unlock itself fails the build fails and says so (and repeats the earlier failure, if there was one): run Unlock Deployment State by hand. One gap: Retrieve Deployment State can put the hold on and then fail, or this build can be aborted while Retrieve Deployment State runs. This build then does not unlock (it cannot tell whether the hold is its own). Read the log of Retrieve Deployment State: if it shows put-object-legal-hold ran, run Unlock Deployment State by hand. If it failed because the hold was already on, do nothing.
Aborting this build is safe (the unlock still runs). When this job was started by HPDS Data - Stage to Stack Bucket, aborting that job only stops its wait: abort this job itself to stop the deployment.
The live stack is never targeted: the build reads environments.next_prod only. A later Deployment Pipeline run rebuilds the staging stack from build-spec.json; the live stack changes only by a stack swap.
IAM: the instance role of this Jenkins needs s3:ListBucket (prefix data/*) and s3:GetObject on data/* in the stack bucket for the check in step 6, besides what Retrieve Deployment State, Unlock Deployment State and the three deploy jobs already use.
The last line of a successful build is "staging stack <name>: HPDS auth, HPDS open, PSAMA deployed".

hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: DATA_S3_OBJECT_KEY
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: Deploy key of the auth dataset: 7 to 40 lowercase hex characters (data/<key>/javabins_rekeyed/ in the stack bucket). Required.

hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: DESTIGMATIZED_DATASET_S3_OBJECT_KEY
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: Deploy key of the open (destigmatized) dataset: 7 to 40 lowercase hex characters (data/<key>/destigmatized_javabins_rekeyed/ in the stack bucket). Required.

hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.name: GENOMIC_DATASET_S3_OBJECT_KEY
hudson.model.StringParameterDefinition.description: Deploy key of the genomic dataset: 7 to 40 lowercase hex characters. Required.
